title: Ops synopsis (concise) — Night -> Morning rotation, 2026-11-02
content:
Overview:
Concise handover from night rotation to morning on-call. Main theme: one transient latency cluster that hit several internal services between 02:13–02:47 UTC and a downstream alerting flurry when the metric exporter lagged. No customer-facing API error rates observed above normal; generation latency tail bumped for a subset of requests serving long-context Llama variants.

Summary highlights:
- Event window: 02:13–02:47 UTC. Peak internal p99 generation latency rose from baseline ~180ms to ~850ms for requests routing to shard-gpu-5 (NVLink pool).
- Root cause hypothesis (so far): KV cache pressure + GC churn on exporter side + slightly misrouted traffic to a newly rolled node with incompatible kernel flags.
- Impact: internal dashboards and some internal tooling (dev CI synthetic runs) reported high latency; customer API 95th remained within SLOs. No 5xx increase observed.
- Pager escalation: one pager at 02:20 for alert SRE-LAT-RED which was acknowledged and handled. No escalation to on-call lead required.

Timeline (concise):
- 01:58 UTC – Minor node replacement completed on shard-gpu-5 (rolling upgrade). No errors in logs at that time.
- 02:13 UTC – Synthetic trace alerts start to show rising generation latency p95/p99. Metric exporter (internal-prom) shows increased scrape timeouts.
- 02:18 UTC – First customer-facing spike check: no correlated 5xx, traffic remained healthy.
- 02:20 UTC – Pager SRE-LAT-RED fired (internal alerting threshold) — on-call ack by me (Ethan). Began targeted sampling on shard-gpu-5.
- 02:24 UTC – Found exporter GC cycles correlating with CPU spikes on monitoring-exporter-7. Restarted exporter pod as mitigation (killed, let deployment recreate).
- 02:30 UTC – Tail sampling: requests with long prompt prefix (~>4096 tokens attempt) ended up missing prefix cache and hit full KV recompute. That path is heavier and created longer GPU kernel queuing.
- 02:33–02:40 UTC – Applied temporary routing rule to divert new long-context requests to shard-gpu-3 which had warmed prefix cache. Observed p99 drop back toward ~300–400ms (not baseline).
- 02:47 UTC – All internal metrics trending back to normal; alert auto-resolved. Left mitigation in place until morning.

What I changed / actions performed (so you don't need to repeat):
- Restarted monitoring-exporter-7 in namespace monitoring to clear GC pressure (logs attached in linked ticket).
- Created routing tweak: traffic-policy override for long-context label to prefer shard-gpu-3 for 6 hours (rollback scheduled unless morning approves longer).
- Opened ticket SRE-312 to investigate kernel flags mismatch and to re-run preflight container kernel config tests on the node that received the rolling upgrade.

Open items / follow-ups for morning on-call (prioritized):
1) Full post-incident trace and correlation (owner: Priya) — collect traces for requests 02:10–02:50, annotate whether cache hit/miss flagged and map to pod IDs. Jira: SRE-312 (in progress).
2) Validate long-context routing policy: ensure canary rollback path is safe; confirm no unexpected capacity imbalance across GPU shards (owner: Marcus).
3) Exporter memory tuning: monitoring-exporter heap flags need revisiting. Add JVM/Go runtime flags to staging image and run soak test (owner: Ethan).
4) Kernel flags audit on shard-gpu-5 node: compare /proc/cmdline and loaded modules with baseline image; escalate to infra if mismatch remains (owner: infra team — linked in ticket).
5) Runbook gap: there is no explicit checklist for "long-context prefix cache warm-up"—I've started a draft runbook page under Confluence (link above). Needs a short checklist and required metrics (owner: eng-sre).

Manual checks for next shift (quick list):
- Confirm routing override still in place or has been rolled back (routing tool: /ops/routing-console, policy id: rp-2026-11-02-lctx).
- Check monitoring-exporter-7 pod memory and GC logs for 24h to confirm no recurring pattern (kubectl logs + Grafana dashboard: Monitoring -> Exporters -> exporter-7).
- Verify GPU shard imbalance: compare active sessions per shard last 12h (Grafana dashboard: Serving -> Shard Utilization).
- Sanity check: run the synthetic long-context job in preprod to confirm warm path on shard-gpu-3 (job id: synth-lctx-20261102-a).

Notes & context (informal):
- Quick hypothesis iteration: the rolling upgrade on shard-gpu-5 likely introduced a subtle kernel param change (maybe disabled a perf counter) that slowed the kernel selection path for certain attention kernels — combined with exporter GC made the effect visible. I don't have definitive proof but the timing lines up.
- We saw no customer-facing errors because traffic steering prevented primary API traffic to the affected shards; this was intentional (traffic-policy stage). Still want a root cause to prevent recurrence.
- The routing override is conservative; it reduces load on shard-gpu-5 but increases utilization on shard-gpu-3 — monitoring thresholds set in the policy will auto-throttle if shard-gpu-3 hits overload.

Runbook drafts / gaps noticed during night triage:
- "Prefix cache warm-up" runbook: outline steps to force warm-up (synthetic request pattern, sequence-length profiles), expected metrics (kv-cache-hit-rate should be >95%), and escalation thresholds.
- "Exporter GC recycling" runbook: when exporter exceeds 70% CPU for 5m AND shows >200ms scrape latency, recommended action is controlled restart + bump memory limit and enable heap profiling.
- Add a small play for identifying kernel-flag mismatches after rolling upgrades — list commands to compare nodes.

Customer / Stakeholder comms:
- No customer-facing incident required. I notified Solutions Eng (Slack #solutions-eng) with a short note and the scripted explanation for possible impact to CI synthetic runs. If we find customer-facing implications after deeper trace, will follow the customer incident comms play.

Useful links / artifacts (quick):
- Tracing samples attached: https://trace.redwood.ai/trace?range=2026-11-02T02:10/02:50
- Jira: SRE-312 (investigate latency spike + runbook)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2314 (related kernel selection tweak currently in review)
- Runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Prefix-Cache-Runbook-v0.9

Closing notes (to morning on-call):
- Please pick up SRE-312 and confirm owner handoff with Priya. If any signs of reemergence (p99 >600ms for >10m) please escalate to on-call lead (pager SRE-LEAD) immediately.
- I'm available on Slack if you want a quick handover walk-through; left timestamps and short playback notes in the ticket.

---
Quick TL;DR: restarted exporter pod, routed long-context to warmed shard to buy time, opened SRE-312 to root cause kernel/rolling-upgrade mismatch and fill runbook gaps. No customer outages observed.

Ethan
